desc.ExpirationInterval: Set a fixed time interval after which administrator privileges expire and revert to standard user rights. A value of 0 disables the timeout and allows the user to request permanent administrator privileges.
desc.ExpirationIntervalMax: Set a maximum time interval for a user to request administrator privileges. This generally works the same way as ExpirationInterval, but allows the user to choose any timeout value up to the specified one. So if the admin would set ExpirationIntervalMax to 20 minutes, the user can choose to set it to a value up to 20 minutes instead of being forced to use the 20 minute timeout.
desc.MaxIntervalInitial: Sets the initial time interval if ExpirationIntervalMax has been configured. If not set and the user never selected an expiration interval, the initial expiration interval is set to 20 minutes. If you want to define an expiration interval that is less than the maximum expiration interval, use this option to define it. As mentioned earlier, this option has no effect if a user has already selected an expiration interval.
desc.AllowPrivilegeRenewal: Specifies whether expiring administrator privileges can be renewed. When enabled, the user will receive a notification one minute before administrator privileges expire. The notification includes a Renew button that can be used to renew administrator privileges.
desc.RenewalFollowsAuthSetting: When enabled, renewing privileges requires the same kind of authentication as initially requesting administrator privileges.
desc.RenewalNotificationInterval: Specifies the number of minutes before the expiration of administrator privileges when Privileges should notify users to renew their privileges. This number must be lower than the expiration interval, otherwise it defaults to 1. If a RenewalCustomAction is specified, its ActionNotificationInterval overwrites the configured interval.
desc.RenewalCustomAction: Specifies a custom action to notify the user about expiring administrator privileges. So you can inform your users using a dialog or whatever you want.
desc.RCA.path: If configured, the default renewal notifications are disabled and the specified executable is launched instead.
desc.RCA.checksum: If set, the PrivilegesAgent calculates the SHA-256 checksum of the binary specified using the ActionExecutablePath option. If the calculated checksum matches the specified one, the binary is executed. Otherwise, the launch operation fails silently, logging only the checksum mismatch.
desc.RCA.interval: This optional value can be configured to specify how many minutes before the admin privileges expire the executable should be launched. If not configured, or the configured value is smaller than 1 or bigger than the expiration interval - 1, it defaults to 1 minute. The notification interval is also passed to the executable configured using ActionExecutablePath as the $1 argument.
desc.AutoRenewalProcessPaths: Specifies the paths to applications/binaries that trigger an automatic renewal of a user’s administrator privileges while they are running. At the specified RenewalNotificationInterval, the PrivilegesAgent checks to see if the user has one of the specified processes running. If so, the administrator privileges are renewed automatically. This feature works independently from the AllowPrivilegeRenewal setting. Therefore, even if you disable privilege renewals for your users, you can still use the automatic renewal feature.
desc.RequireAuthentication: Specifies whether authentication is required to obtain administrator privileges. When enabled, the user is prompted for the account password (or Touch ID, if available).
desc.RequireBiometricAuthentication: Specifies whether biometric authentication is required to obtain administrator privileges. When enabled, the PrivilegesAgent prompts the user for Touch ID and does not offer an alternative option. If Touch ID is unavailable or has not been configured, the user is prompted for their account password instead.
desc.BiometricsFallbackType: This specifies the fallback strategy when RequireBiometricAuthentication is enabled. By default, users are prompted to enter their username and password if biometric authentication is not configured or is unavailable. However, this may not be the desired behavior in all environments.
hint.BiometricsFallbackType: PrivilegesCLI does not use biometric authentication by default. Therefore, this setting will be ignored unless the AllowCLIBiometricAuthentication setting is enabled.
desc.AllowCLIBiometricAuthentication: Specifies whether to allow biometric authentication (or smart cards) in the PrivilegesCLI to obtain administrator privileges. When enabled, the authentication process is passed to PrivilegesAgent, which then prompts the user for Touch ID or smart card. If neither of these are available, the user is prompted for the account password.
desc.EnableSmartCardSupport: Specifies whether to enable smart card support for authentication. Since the modern Local Authentication framework does not yet support smart cards/PIV tokens, enabling this option will cause the application to fall back to the older Authorization Services. Enabling this option will disable RequireBiometricAuthentication.
hint.EnableSmartCardSupport: PrivilegesCLI does not use smart card authentication by default. To enable it, please make sure the AllowCLIBiometricAuthentication setting is also enabled.
desc.LimitToUser: Restricts use of the application to the specified user or list of users. When used with a client management system that supports variables in configuration profiles, variables such as $USERNAME can be used here.
desc.LimitToGroup: Restricts use of the application to the specified group or list of groups.
desc.RevokePrivilegesAtLogin: When enabled, the user’s administrator privileges are revoked at login.
hint.RevokePrivilegesAtLogin: For those who use fixed admin accounts on their machines: If you want to enable this feature, please make sure you exclude the admin account(s) using the RevokeAtLoginExcludedUsers key. Otherwise these accounts become standard user accounts at next log in.
desc.RevokeAtLoginExcludedUsers: If RevokePrivilegesAtLogin is enabled, the specified users are excluded from privilege revocation at login. When used with a client management system that supports variables in configuration profiles, variables such as $USERNAME can be used here.
desc.RevokePrivilegesAfterSystemTimeChan: When enabled, the user’s administrator privileges are revoked if the system time did change. Enable this feature to prevent users from extending their admin time by adjusting the time on their Mac.
desc.RevokeAfterTimeChangeExcludedUsers: If RevokePrivilegesAfterSystemTimeChange is enabled, the specified users are excluded from privilege revocation after system time did change. When used with a client management system that supports variables in configuration profiles, variables such as $USERNAME can be used here.
desc.RevokePrivilegesOnScreenLock: When enabled, the user’s administrator privileges are revoked whenever the screen is locked.
desc.RevokeOnScreenLockExcludedUsers: If RevokePrivilegesOnScreenLock is enabled, the specified users are excluded from privilege revocation on screen lock. When used with a client management system that supports variables in configuration profiles, variables such as $USERNAME can be used here.
desc.AutomaticRevocationExcludedUsers: The specified users are excluded from any automatic revocation. This key is evaluated before the keys RevokeAtLoginExcludedUsers, RevokeAfterTimeChangeExcludedUsers, RevokeOnScreenLockExcludedUsers, and any other automatic revocation key that may be introduced in the future. If a user is listed in the AutomaticRevocationExcludedUsers key, the other keys are not evaluated. When used with a client management system that supports variables in configuration profiles, variables such as $USERNAME can be used here.
desc.ReasonRequired: When enabled, the user must provide a reason for requesting administrator privileges. The reason is logged. Note that once this option is enabled, privileges cannot be changed from the Privileges Dock tile menu or the status item menu.
desc.ReasonMinLength: If ReasonRequired is enabled, this key specifies the minimum number of characters the user has to enter as the reason for becoming an admin. If not set, the value defaults to 10. If a value < 1 is specified or if ReasonMinLength is > 250, the value is set to default.
desc.ReasonMaxLength: If ReasonRequired is enabled, this key specifies the maximum number of characters the user can enter as the reason for becoming an admin. If not set, the value defaults to 250. If a value > 250 is specified or if ReasonMaxLength is <= ReasonMinLength, the value is set to default.
desc.ReasonCheckingEnabled: When enabled, the text the user enters for a reason is roughly parsed for valid words. If the text does not contain any valid words, the Request Privileges button remains grayed out, even if the minimum number of characters has been entered. The test passes if the text contains any valid words, even if they don’t make sense.
hint.ReasonCheckingEnabled: This feature is experimental and disabled by default. If you enable it, please check carefully that it works as expected in your environment.
desc.PassReasonToExecutable: Specifies whether the reason that the user entered when requesting administrator privileges should be passed to the executable configured with the PostChangeExecutablePath key. This is disabled by default. If enabled, the reason is passed to the executable as $3.
desc.ReasonPresetList: This key allows to pre-define a list of possible reasons (for becoming an admin) the user can choose from. When set, an additional pop-up menu will appear in the dialog box. This only works for the GUI version of Privileges.
desc.ReasonStrictPresetList: When enabled, the ReasonPresetList is used as defined, otherwise an additional entry Other… is added to the list of presets allowing the users to enter a custom reason for requesting admin rights.
desc.PostChangeExecutablePath: When set, the PrivilegesAgent executes the given application or script and provides the current user’s user name ($1) and its privileges (admin or user, $2) as launch arguments. If the application or script does not exist or is not executable, the launch operation fails silently.
desc.PostChangeExecutableChecksum: If set, the PrivilegesAgent calculates the SHA-256 checksum of the binary specified using the PostChangeExecutablePath option. If the calculated checksum matches the specified one, the binary is executed. Otherwise, the launch operation fails silently, logging only the checksum mismatch.
desc.PostChangeActionOnGrantOnly: When enabled, the application or script, specified in PostChangeExecutablePath, will only be executed if administrator privileges are granted to a user, but not the privileges are revoked.
desc.HideOtherWindows: By default, Privileges hides open windows to show the desktop and ensure that only the Privileges window is visible on the screen. Set HideOtherWindows to false to disable this function.
desc.HideSettingsButton: When enabled, the Settings button is no longer displayed in the app.
desc.HideSettingsFromDockMenu: When enabled, the Settings menu item is no longer displayed in the Dock tile’s menu.
desc.HideSettingsFromStatusItem: When enabled, the Settings menu item is no longer displayed in the status item’s menu.
desc.HideHelpButton: When enabled, the Help (?) button is no longer displayed in the app.
desc.HelpButtonCustomURL: If specified, this url is called instead of the Privileges GitHub url if the user clicks the help button. Malformed urls and non-http(s) urls are ignored.
desc.ShowInMenuBar: When enabled, a Privileges status item is displayed in the Menu Bar.
desc.ShowRemainingTimeInMenuBar: When enabled, a timer displaying the remaining admin time is shown in the Privileges status item.
desc.UsagePolicy: If specified, a usage policy will be displayed the first time the user requests administrator privileges. The user must acknowledge it before proceeding. The PrivilegesCLI command-line tool cannot be used to request administrator privileges until the Privileges application has been launched and the usage policy has been accepted.
desc.ForceUpdatePrebootVolume: When enabled, the PrivilegesDaemon runs the command /usr/sbin/diskutil apfs updatePreboot / whenever a user’s privileges change. You should normally never have to enable this function because the preboot volume is updated automatically after a while. However, we implemented this feature because it seems to be needed in some environments.
hint.ForceUpdatePrebootVolume: Please only enable this function if you know precisely why you are doing so.
desc.EnableSystemExtension: When enabled, the Privileges system extension is enabled. The system extension protects the Privileges application and its components against unauthorized modifications, deactivation, or uninstallation. Once this key has been set, it is no longer possible to enable or disable the extension using PrivilegesCLI.
hint.EnableSystemExtension: The Privileges system extension requires macOS 13 or newer. Please make sure you grant the extension (corp.sap.privileges.extension) full disk access, otherwise it will not work.
desc.RemoteLogging: Configures remote logging settings for the Privileges application.
desc.RL.serverType: At the moment syslog and webhook are the only supported values.
desc.RL.serverAddress.syslog: Please provide an ip address or a fully-qualified domain name (FQDN).
desc.RL.queueUnsentEvents: When enabled, syslog and webhook events that could not be sent are queued. When a user changes privileges, PrivilegesAgent attempts to resend these events. The maximum number of queued events can be set using the QueuedEventsMax key. If not set, a maximum of 20 events will be queued.
desc.RL.queuedEventsMax: Specifies the maximum number of queued events. If not set, a maximum of 20 events will be queued. When set to 0, an unlimited number of events will be queued.
desc.RL.serverPort: If not specified, the port defaults to 514 or to 6514 if TLS is enabled.
desc.RL.useTLS: When enabled, TLS is enabled for the connection. Please make sure your clients have a certificate installed that matches Apple’s requirements.
desc.RL.logFacility: If not specified, facility defaults to 4 (security).
desc.RL.logSeverity: If not specified, severity defaults to 6 (informational).
desc.RL.maxMessageSize: If not specified, the value defaults to 480 which is the minimum maximum message size a syslog server must support. If the syslog message is larger than the specified maximum, the message will be truncated at the end.
desc.RL.messageFormat: If not specified, the value defaults to 1, which describes an RFC 5424 compliant syslog message that uses non-transparent framing. Set this value to 2 if you want to create RFC 5424 compliant syslog messages that use octet counting.
desc.RL.structuredData: Each SD element contains an SD id (which is the name of the element in the form of a string) and SD parameters. SD parameters are defined in a dictionary. The values of this dictionary must be of type string. Keys must be US-ASCII. Spaces and some special characters are not allowed.
desc.RL.webhookCustomData: You may use this dictionary to pass custom data (like the machine name, serial number, Jamf Pro ID, etc.) to the webhook. This data is added to the webhook’s JSON as custom_data.
opt.BiometricsFallbackType.0: Ask for credentials if biometrics are unavailable or unconfigured
opt.BiometricsFallbackType.1: Ask only if biometrics are unavailable (not if unconfigured)
